clauses.mechanism: own terms: sunset date, restriction of competition runs until July 25, 1952 (recorded inclusive)
clauses.reason: The sole clause restricts competition in examinations for Substitute Railway Postal Clerk, in the words that run "July 25, 1952, to persons" entitled to preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944, "as long as" persons so entitled are available. The order's own end date is July 25, 1952. It is recorded inclusive, so the restriction runs through the end of July 25, 1952; the exclusive reading would have it end when that day begins, so that July 24, 1952 is the last day. The second paragraph, which directs replacement of incumbents who fail to qualify, depends on the order being applicable and ends with the restriction. The signature date is "August 28, 1947." and the order is not conditioned on any act that could have ended it sooner except the availability of preference eligibles, which no held source dates. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. No held text extends, amends or revokes it.

research_rationale:
EO 9889 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9889.txt, 12 FR 5831, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order restricts competition in civil service examinations for the position of Substitute Railway Postal Clerk to persons entitled to veterans' preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944 until July 25, 1952, as long as persons entitled to preference are available, with provisos on classification and on status for non-preference employees, and directs replacement of incumbents who do not qualify. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms fix the date to which the restriction runs.

savings.reason: The order authorized the Civil Service Commission to confer a competitive civil service status or a probational status on a qualifying incumbent who had served continuously since the date of the order; status so conferred before the restriction ended is an accrued consequence. No held source continues the restriction or the replacement direction after July 25, 1952.
